delta.notes: With-skill produces larger, more structured outputs. Pass rate identical at 100% — assertions are not discriminating. Key differences are qualitative: wikilinks, YAML-list tags, structured frontmatter, Obsidian compatibility, web research.

analyst_observations: All assertions pass for both configurations — they test structural basics (frontmatter, TOC, links) which both Claude versions produce correctly
With-skill outputs are consistently larger: 1035 vs 936 lines (JMM), 785 vs 589 lines (VT) — ~19% more content on average
With-skill uses YAML-list tags and wikilinks (Obsidian graph), without-skill uses JSON-array tags and markdown links
With-skill JMM includes VarHandle, memory barriers table, and web-researched sources; without-skill misses some depth
With-skill VT references JEP 491 (JDK 24 pinning fix) and JEP 505/506 — more current information from web search
Token usage is higher for with-skill (+59%) due to web search and skill reading overhead
Qualitative review by human is essential — structural assertions don't capture content depth or accuracy
